You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Gift of Tulips In Gift of Tulips, tulip enthusiasts explore Amsterdam's tulip festival to build colorful bouquets, give tulips to others (scoring points in the process), and manipulate the value of the tulips in the festival. The deck includes tulips of four colors, with values 2-4. Lay out four Festival cards based on the player count, with these cards showing the number of points scored for giving away tulips, keeping tulips, and having a majority of certain colors at the end of the game. On a turn, draw a card from the deck and KEEP/GIVE/ADD it, then draw a second card and take one of the actions you didn't just take. Whoever has the most points at the end of the game wins. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Game Setup 2 How to Play 3 Strategy 4 End of Game Game Setup Remove cards based on the current player count: 2: 18 cards plus the 24 5/6P cards 3: 4 plus the 24 5/6P cards 4: 6 plus the 24 5/6P cards 5: 14 cards 6: 10 cards Draw two Tulip cards and add them to the Festival. Deal two cards to each player. Each player places one card into their bouquet and the other card into the Secret Festival. How to Play On your turn, you will draw a Tulip card and take an action, then draw another Tulip and take a DIFFERENT action. Possible actions Add the Tulip to your Bouquet. Gain points if the Tulip is ranked 3 rd or 4 th . Give the Tulip to a Friend. Gain points based on the Tulip's value plus its current giving value. Place the tulip into the Festival (your choice between the Regular or Secret Festival). The rank of a Tulip in the Festival is based on total value of all Tulips with the same color. If, after playing a card, the total value is ever equal to other tulip color(s), it is placed higher than these other colors in the Festival. Strategy Gift Tulips Strategically: Target Tulips ranked 1st or 2nd in the Festival for gifting. Optimal scenarios for gifting include: Opponent's Tulip Lead: Gift when your opponent has a significant lead in the Tulip count for a specific color. Higher chances of scoring (5 to 8 points) compared to aiming for bouquet majority. Your Tulip Lead: Gift when you have a substantial lead in the Tulip count for a specific color. Lower risk of the opponent surpassing your lead, providing an opportunity for extra points. Secret Festival Placement: Add Tulips to the Secret Festival where you have the majority. This increases the likelihood of elevating the rank of that color at the game's end. Keeps opponents unaware of your strategy, providing a strategic advantage. Festival Addition: Add Tulips to the Festival toward the end of the game, especially when you are confident about having the majority in a specific color. Ensures maximum points for that color and solidifies your position as the game concludes End of Game The game ends when the deck runs out. Up to five cards are then drawn from the Secret Festival and added to the Festival, changing the Tulip ranking in the progress. Then, for each Tulip color, players receive the points listed on the Festival cards for having the first, second or third majority of Tulip cards in their bouquet in that color. In case of a tie, the player with the higher total value of Tulip cards gets the points. In case of another tie, both players get the listed amount of points for that majority. A third player will then gets points for the following majority etc. The player with the most points wins the game. If tied, the player with the most Tulips wins the game. When again tied, players share the victory! [Rating: 3.5/10] The art is gorgeous and there is a neat mechanism there with sending the currently winning cards to your opponents for points, or keeping them hoping they'll pay off, or sending them to the festival to improve how much that suit is worth. I got excited looking at the rules, like a King of Siam (a.k.a. King is Dead) kind of thing.  Sadly the actual gameplay just has you flipping one card at a time, making a decision that's VERY simple after the first turn or two, and then repeating until someone wins based purely on luck if people aren't misplaying terribly. [Rating: 4/10] I backed this on Kickstarter and was excited for this one because I love flowers. Unfortunately, I just don't see any appeal to the gameplay. I've played about 6 times with multiple player counts (2, 4, and 6) and each time I found myself completely bored doing the same actions over and over and watching my opponent(s) doing the same actions over and over. Not for me.

[Rating: 4/10] This one felt too complicated to me, for what was ultimately a fairly simple game. We played in a dimly lit room as well - and as gorgeous as the illustrations were, it was hard to tell the colors apart. In addition, because the cards are top-decked and decisions are made one-at-a-time (as each card is revealed), it made for a slow play with certain AP-prone players.

[Rating: 4/10] A stock-holding game where you can gift shares to other players for immediate points instead of working towards the big endgame payout. The game doesn't really work well because the cost/payout ratios of the different actions depend so heavily on the random card draw that there is pretty little agency and it all comes down to chance.
